title.narrative: Executive Program: Developing Care and Innovation in Maternal and Child Health

description.narrative: The overall objective of the project is to: - Contribute to the reduction of preventable maternal and newborn mortality and morbidity in Yemen through the implementation of evidence-based maternal, newborn, and child health and nutrition products and interventions. - Support 29 healthcare facilities with medical equipment, supplies, laboratory consumables, intensive care equipment, and emergency kits. - Provide project operating budgets and incentives for medical staff. Training Yemeni personnel on modern technologies.

The project represents a strategic collaboration between the King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre (KSrelief), the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation (GF), and International Medical Corps (IMC) to pilot innovative interventions that address critical maternal, newborn, and child health needs and challenges in Yemen. By leveraging our combined resources and expertise, this partnership aims to achieve significant improvements in maternal and newborn health outcomes in Yemen. The goal is to scale up successful maternal and newborn interventions regionally and globally, based on the empirical evidence provided by this proposed pilot project. These interventions will contribute to accelerating country-specific and global commitments related to Sustainable Development Goal 3 – to reduce maternal, neonatal, and child mortality and morbidity.

The project will contribute to the diagnosis of a number of diseases, including: - Reducing premature infant mortality - Reducing maternal mortality - Supporting the resilience of the health sector - Treating patients with chronic diseases - Equipping and establishing intensive care and emergency departments in six central hospitals.
